requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test source only and did not request implementation source. The tests adequately cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fingerprints`.

- **SHA-256 digest of the word-based encoding.**
  - `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` checks that the Markdown fingerprint is a 64-character hex string.
  - The same test and `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` check that `two words` and `twowords` differ while whitespace changes do not.
  - The tests do not compare against a known SHA-256 value. A 64-hex-digit digest with this behaviour is a reasonable check of the clause.

- **Fingerprint scheme.** This is cited context, so I did not reassess it. `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` also asserts that `Markdown.fingerprint_scheme()` is `markdown-structural-v1`. It also checks that loaded contents retain that scheme.

- **HTML comment blocks are excluded.**
  - `comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile` has a Markdown case. Changing the block comment's text, or deleting the block, leaves the `section[H]` hash unchanged. Changing a prose word changes it.
  - `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` has a similar Markdown case.
  - `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` shows that only the block counts as a comment.

- **Inline HTML comments are ordinary paragraph text.**
  - `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` changes the text of an inline `<!-- one -->` comment to `two`, and the section hash changes.
  - `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` shows the owning node is a `paragraph`.

- **Reflowing whitespace within a paragraph preserves the hash; changing words changes it.**
  - `reflowing_markdown_paragraphs_keeps_the_hash` shows that moving the line break or joining the lines leaves the hash unchanged, while `brownfox` changes it.
  - `markdown_hashes_include_paragraph_text_between_punctuation_tokens` shows that adding the word `now` changes the hash, and that extra spaces do not.
  - `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` has Markdown cases for both.
  - `anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates` shows the nested directive and paragraph hash survives reflow, and that changed words change the hash.

- **Directive prose uses word-based hashing.** `directive_prose_hashes_words_across_reflow_without_joining_them` checks a directive node. Reflowing keeps the fingerprint, and joining `two words` into `twowords` changes the structural hash.

I found no obligation or named boundary case that lacks a test with an assertion on its outcome.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore

/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
